definitions.explanation: A genetic phenomenon where a trait from a grandparent or earlier ancestor reappears in a descendant, having skipped one or more intervening generations. Also used colloquially to describe personality traits or talents that seem inherited from grandparents.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{隔世遺伝|かくせいいでん}⟦かもしれない→かもしれない：00164_kamoshirenai⟧。
examples.english: This personality trait might be a case of skipping a generation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{似|に}ている→似る：01159_niru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{隔世遺伝|かくせいいでん}だろう⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: I wonder if my resemblance to my grandfather is atavism.

examples.japanese: ⟦{絵|え}→絵：02613_e⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{才能|さいのう}→才能：02772_sainou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦なかった→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{画家|がか}→画家：02583_gaka⟧だった⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{隔世遺伝|かくせいいでん}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: My father had no artistic talent, but since my grandmother was a painter, people say it's a case of skipping a generation.

notes:
USAGE:
{隔世|かくせい} means "a generation apart" and ⟦{遺伝|いでん}→遺伝：10137_iden⟧ means "heredity". A biology term, but common in everyday talk whenever a child takes after a grandparent rather than a parent, in looks, character or talent.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {隔世遺伝|かくせいいでん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{似|に}ている→似る：01159_niru⟧ (to take after one's grandfather, skipping a generation)
- {隔世遺伝|かくせいいでん}⟦かもしれない→かもしれない：00164_kamoshirenai⟧ (it might have skipped a generation)
